title: Disk quotas
subtitle: Per-user and per-group space and inode caps — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Limit how much disk a user or group may use; alert an admin before someone fills a partition
cards.example: cap a user’s mail/home separately from a project group
cards.notes: Apply to individual users and user groups.

cards.example: person’s home vs project group space
cards.notes: You can cap a person’s mail and home separately from a project group they belong to.

cards.example: stop one user from filling the partition
cards.notes: One of two resources you can limit (the other is inodes).

cards.meaning: Limits the number of files/directories that can be created
cards.example: millions of tiny files → “disk full” with free gigabytes
cards.notes: Inodes store file metadata — inode exhaustion is a classic failure mode.

cards.meaning: Warning / grace period — user can temporarily exceed before hard enforcement
cards.example: soft limit on blocks or inodes
cards.notes: Contrast hard limit = cannot go beyond.

cards.example: writes fail once hard limit is hit

Show quota for the current (or named) user
cards.notes: User-facing report; admins also use repquota.

cards.meaning: usrquota/grpquota in fstab → quotacheck → quotaon → edquota/setquota → repquota/quota
cards.notes: Know the names; flags come with practice.

cards.meaning: Shared /home or mail, build agents filling /var or /tmp, multi-tenant hosts and inode exhaustion
cards.example: one intern’s core dump should not page the whole team
cards.notes: Tiny log files can exhaust inodes on jump hosts.
